_note: ASSET SEAM (PLAN.md 2.1). The only file mapping a visual ID to a path.
No filename appears in gameplay code -- everything goes through
GameDataRegistry.atlas_for().
Every ID carries BOTH an atlas path and a placeholder. atlas_for() prefers
the atlas and silently falls back to the placeholder when it is absent, so
the game runs identically whether or not the art pack is mounted (PLAN.md
3.2). That is why placeholders ship in the APK permanently rather than
being deleted once art lands.
Atlas paths point into res://assets/atlases/, which is where the downloaded
pack mounts via load_resource_pack() (0.3). Nothing is committed there yet,
so today every ID resolves to its placeholder.
footprint_m and height_m are METRES, not pixels -- see placeholder_spec.gd
for why. Every figure below is measured, via `isobake inspect` on the source
actor, halved (inspect reports raw 0 A.D. units and the pipeline's
tile-to-tile factor is 0.5). Heights subtract the buried skirt where there is
one, per ASSET_MISSING.md 1.2: the town centre loses 2.7 m, the 3x3 rubble
1.8, the house 0.7. Note the rubble and foundation footprints are LARGER than
the buildings they belong to -- 0 A.D. authors them that way, rubble spreads
and a foundation pad oversizes its building -- so they are not typos.
SKINS (PLAN.md 2.7.1). An entry may carry two OPTIONAL axes on top of its
base `atlas`, and atlas_for(id, age, colour) composes them:
"ages":    { "1": path, "2": path, "3": path, "4": path }
"colours": true
`ages` is DENSE by contract -- every age names a skin explicitly, and two
ages that look the same simply point at the SAME baked atlas. That is why a
building that cannot be built until age 2 still names an age-1 entry: it
points at the age-2 art, the branch is never taken, and the file answers
"what does this look like in age 3?" by being read rather than by tracing
an inheritance chain. _validate_skins() fails the suite on a gap.
`colours` is a FLAG, not a map, and it is the one place the two axes are
treated differently. Age is a judgement -- which bake serves which age is a
decision per building, and worth writing down. Player colour is mechanical:
isobake emits vis.<id>.<colour> for each of colours.json's eight slots, so
the path is derivable and eight declared paths per unit would be eight
chances to typo one. A tint with no file staged falls back to the untinted
bake; GameDataRegistry.missing_colour_atlases() is what makes that findable,
since an untinted unit belongs to no player and colour is the ONLY thing
telling players apart (PLAN.md 1).
THREE THINGS DELIBERATELY LACK `colours`, and none is an oversight:
vis.dragon is bespoke art with no playercolor mask at all; vis.ballista is a
0 A.D. siege engine, and NO siege engine there carries player colour -- every
siege_* actor uses no_trans_parallax_spec over siege_artillery_01.png, and
artillery colour lives on the separate crew actors. vis.onager only tints
because siege_onager_pivot happens to mount crew props that carry a mask,
and the lithobolos mounts none that do -- its eight tint passes measured
0.0%, i.e. eight identical atlases, so claiming the flag would mean eight
copies of one picture and a resolution path that looks like it worked.
vis.siege_ram predates that finding but does bake eight visibly distinct
pages, so it keeps the flag.
BUILDINGS HAVE NO COLOUR BAKES YET and so carry no `colours` flag. 0 A.D.
structures do declare a playercolor mask, but only units and ships have been
baked per colour so far. Adding the flag here is all that is needed the day
they are -- vis.town_center_age3.blue falls out of the same two steps.
town_center AND house WERE RE-MEASURED 2026-08-16, and their old figures are
worth keeping in view: 15.5 x 15.0 m / 6.8 m and 10.0 x 10.0 m / 6.6 m. Those
came from `isobake inspect` at 0.4 against the ATHENIAN actors, which is what
was staged then. The roster puts age 1 on the BRITONS (Age & Unit Planning.md)
and the bake was re-pointed accordingly -- the Briton town centre projects
315 px wide against the Athenian one's 459 -- so both figures had quietly
stopped describing the art. Nothing reported it, because a placeholder is only
drawn when the atlas is absent and both atlases were present, just different.
The lesson is the one already recorded for vis.villager: a placeholder is an
INDEPENDENT statement of intended size, so it goes stale silently unless it is
re-derived whenever its bake is re-pointed.
Every figure below, those two now included, is derived from its own baked
atlas rather than from
`isobake inspect`, which is on the art side of the fence. The projection is
invertible, so this is measurement and not estimation: Iso projects a
footprint of (fx, fy) metres to a diamond (fx + fy) * 16 px wide, and puts
the sprite's top (fx + fy) * 4 + height * 19.596 px above the anchor. So
fx + fy = rect.w / 16 and height = (anchor.y - rect.w / 4) / 19.596, with the
x:y split taken from the source template's obstruction aspect. Checked
against the villager, whose atlas this reads as 2.0 m against her measured
2.18 -- close enough to trust, and the residual is the sprite's own padding.
stone_mine, sheep and cattle were derived that way on 2026-08-17, when they
were finally wired (all three had been staged and referenced by nothing).
For the two ANIMALS the frame matters: an S-facing beast is drawn head-on, so
its S rect.w gives its WIDTH and not its length. Their footprints come from
the E frame, which shows the animal side-on, and their heights from the S
frame, where the whole animal is above the anchor. Taking both from S would
have declared a 0.9 m sheep -- shorter than it is long.
THE ORE SET LANDED the same day, and it moved two of these a long way. The
roster's own actors replaced two off-roster stand-ins, and the size classes now
pick the SPRITE as well as the amount (resources.json `visuals`):
vis.gold_mine    64x60 px -> 180x119   was metalmine_alpine, a pale spire
vis.stone_mine  222x191 px ->  72x62   was stonemine_medit_quarry
So gold grew about 3x and stone shrank about 3x, and both anchors moved -- the
figures below are re-derived, and the ones they replaced (2.8 x 3.87 / 1.21 and
6.94 x 6.94 / 5.78) described art that is gone. The art side flagged the
re-measure rather than leaving it to be found, which is the vis.villager lesson
being applied from the other end of the fence.
The gold LARGE reads 0.24 m tall, which looks like a mistake and is not: the
square Aegean seam is a flat quarry patch 244 px wide and barely raised. PLAN.md
13.2 item 7 has the background -- these newer sculpts are authored half-sunk
into terrain (47% of the round gold below the ground plane, 64% of the square),
which 0 A.D. hides behind terrain occlusion and an orthographic bake cannot.
They were unusable until isobake grew render.ground_clip; that item is closed.
THE FOUR TREES were re-derived together, and the oak's old 2.4 x 2.4 / 10.0 is
the last figure in this file that came from the inspect-halved convention. It
had to move because the four species are now variants of each other: comparing
a 2.4 m oak against a 5.53 m elm would read as one of them being wrong when the
difference was only which method measured it.
A building that re-skins across ages gets ONE placeholder, sized to the MAX
of its skins per axis, for the same reason its footprint is (buildings.json):
it re-skins in place and cannot change size underneath the player.
VARIANTS (2026-08-17), a THIRD optional axis and the only one that is not a
skin:
"variants": ["vis.field_1", "vis.field_2", ...]
A list of other visual IDS, not paths, that are interchangeable looks for the
same thing. GameDataRegistry.variant_of(id, seed) picks one; every entry named
in the list is an ordinary declaration in its own right, so nothing downstream
-- atlas_for, the staleness scan, the portraits -- learns a new concept.
Why IDS and not a list of paths on one entry: a path list would need a fourth
argument threaded through atlas_for, its cache key, and EntityView, to express
something the id namespace already expresses for free.
The distinction from `ages` is the point. An age skin is the SAME building
looking different because the player advanced -- it changes under a standing
building, and which bake serves which age is a judgement. A variant is a
different-but-equal look chosen once, when the thing is built, and never
revisited. Fields are the first of these: the project owner's four plots are
four crops, not four ages, and a plot does not re-sow itself when Rome
arrives. `ages` and `variants` on one entry would therefore be a contradiction
and _validate_skins() rejects it.
The four field FILES are still named vis.field_age2/3/4 and vis.farm, because
that is what the art side baked before we knew they were variants. The ids do
not follow them and must not be renamed to match: the whole purpose of this
file is that ids outlive filenames. Renaming the staged files would also be
undone by the next run of the art agent's staging script, which is theirs.
vis.field's own placeholder was re-derived at the same time. It read 3.88 m
against art that projects 534 px, i.e. 16.7 -- stale in exactly the way the
vis.villager lesson above describes, and it had been wrong since the plots were
last re-pointed.
VARIANT POOLS (2026-08-28), a refinement of `variants` and not a fourth axis:
"variant_pools": { "island": [ids], "forest": [...], "river": [...],
"desert": [...] }
A pool is a `variants` list that only applies on one KIND OF MAP. The keys are
MapGenerator's own type names lowercased -- MapGenerator.pool_name() is the one
place that spelling is decided, and pool_names() is what _validate_variants
checks against, so a typo'd biome fails the suite instead of silently never
resolving. GameView carries the resolved pool (map meta `type`) and passes it to
variant_of(); a view that has not been told one -- the fixed debug map, every
preview, every test -- falls back to the plain `variants` list, which is why oak
/ elm / toona stay declared there rather than being folded into `forest`.
WHICH SPECIES GO IN WHICH POOL IS THE PROJECT OWNER'S ASSIGNMENT, recorded on
line 1 of each recipe in tools/recipes/tree_*.toml ('-- forest pool', and
palm_date's '-- island+river pool', which is why one id appears in two lists).
Do not re-derive it from how a tree looks.
vis.tree_banyan IS EXCLUDED, and that is now a DECISION rather than a pending
question (project owner, 2026-08-28: 'the test scene confirms the warning, the
tree will not work, please exclude it'). It projects 336-370 px wide against the
250 band -- worse than the teak pulled on 2026-08-23 -- and the owner reproduced
the teak's actual defect with it in dev_preview/preview_banyan.tscn, which is a
playable grove rather than a picture: the canopy covers ground the entity does
not own, so a tap meant for one thing lands on another.
It stays DECLARED and in no pool, on purpose. The declaration is what lets the
preview draw it, and the preview is the tool for the next tree somebody wants to
add. Nothing gathers it, because a pool is the only thing that puts a species on
the map. THE RULE THIS SETTLES, so the next big tree needs no round trip: the
250 px band is not a guideline about looks, it is the width at which a tree stops
being tappable next to its neighbours. Two species have now failed it.
THE THIRTEEN NEW TREES were derived by the inversion above, from the N FRAME.
N and not the widest, and not S: the four trees already here were measured that
way and it reproduces all eight of their declared figures exactly (7.25/8.03,
5.53/13.08, 8.53/13.54, 6.16/9.42). A tree is near enough radially symmetric
that the choice is arbitrary, but a MIXED convention would show up as one
species reading a metre wider than its neighbour for no reason -- which is the
same trap the oak's re-derivation note above records.
THE FIVE CARCASSES ARE THE ONE PLACE THAT INVERSION DOES NOT WORK, and it fails
loudly enough to be worth writing down: run on a collapsed body it returns a
NEGATIVE height for four of the five (the wolf's E frame gives -0.35 m). The
formula assumes the sprite's top is the subject's top, and a carcass lies below
its own anchor. The art side hit the same wall from their end -- deer_carcass
derives 2.47 m, taller than the standing deer -- and shipped 0.90 by eye.
So the five are the DEER CARCASS'S OWN PROPORTIONS applied to each animal's
measured live figures: length kept, the short axis widened x1.7, height 45% of
standing -- which is what [1.6, 0.7] / 2.02 -> [1.6, 1.2] / 0.90 already was.
An animal lying down covers the ground it stood on, and a bear's body is bigger
than a wolf's, which a straight frame-crop measurement of these sprites does not
agree with (both crop to 58 px). They affect the selection ring and
Occlusion.column_pad_for's outline band, and nothing else. asset_request.md's
[P5] carries the ask for real measurements.
THERE IS NO FACING FLAG HERE, and one was tried and taken out again on
2026-08-22. `directions_reversed` set a half-turn offset on the 31 entries whose
recipes lack `yaw_offset_deg = 180.0` -- every unit, ship, animal and siege
engine is baked 180 degrees from the direction its atlas labels. It fixed idle
and walk and did NOT fix attacking, which is where the owner had reported it, so
they called it: the defect is in the recipes and the fix belongs in the bake
(PLAN.md 13.2 item 10, asset_request.md carries the request). Do not re-add it
without an answer for the attack clip -- the same patch failing twice is worse
than the bug, which at least is honest about being an art problem.
_note_walls: WALLS (PLAN.md 5.8). Staged since the wall bakes landed and DECLARED HERE
2026-08-21 -- buildings.json used to claim they were already declared in this
file, and they were not: only the tower's rubble and foundation were. That is
why nothing rendered a wall and nothing failed either; an undeclared id is not
an error, it resolves to the loud magenta placeholder, and no building def
pointed at one to make it appear.
THREE TIERS, EACH RE-SKINNING BY AGE, per the roster's wall lines and the
project owner's call (2026-08-21): a player at age 4 may still build any of the
three, so these are three separate ladders rather than one ladder's rungs.
tier         age 1     age 2     age 3     age 4      roster line
wood         brit      brit      brit      brit       'wall Lumber'
stone        achae     achae     achae     achae      'wall Stone'
reinforced   rome      rome      rome      rome       'wall reinforced'
THE WOOD ROW USED TO READ germ germ brit brit and the project owner flattened
it on 2026-08-28. The two bakes are not a re-skin of one wall, they are two
different walls -- the germ palisade (`_age2`) is dark planks with pointed posts
and a roofed gatehouse, the brit one (`_age3`) is a lower wall on a stone footing
with playercolour banners -- so advancing an age silently replaced walls the
player had already built with a different structure.
THE BRIT WALL IS THE ONE THEY WANTED, and the file suffix is why it took two
goes: the owner asked for 'only (age2) wood walls & gate for both', meaning the
wall they had been looking at in age 2 -- which was the brit one, because the
row above still put brit at age 3 and they had advanced. So `_age2` in that
sentence is a game age and `_age2` in a filename is the 0 A.D. phase the mesh
came from, and the two do not have to name the same wall. They now do: the wood
tier is brit at every age. The germ bakes stay staged and unused, like the
Athenian set below.
Ages below a tier's `age_required` still name an atlas because the skin map is
DENSE BY CONTRACT (PLAN.md 2.7.1) and `_validate_skins()` fails the suite on a
gap -- they simply point at the earliest bake, and the building gate is what
stops anyone seeing them there. That is now also why the wood tier repeats one
path four times rather than dropping the map: the contract is dense, and a tier
that does not change with the age says so by repeating itself.
EIGHT DIRECTIONS, unlike every other building. Wall segments are the first
building in the project with `directions: 8` -- SimBuilding's header says
buildings have no facing and every building atlas is a single frame, and walls
are the exception that gave SimBuilding a `facing` field. A wall has to run
along whichever axis it was dragged on, so the art was baked rotated and the
sim stores which rotation. Only two of the eight are reachable today, because
the footprint system is axis-aligned; four more are their 180-degree twins and
draw the same symmetric wall, and the last two are the true diagonals.
WHICH TWO, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the sprite baked as SW is the wall
lying along tile axis X and SE is the one lying along axis Y -- a wall faces
ACROSS its own length, not along it. Every wall, gate, foundation and rubble
atlas here agrees, old bakes and new. `WallPlan.FACING_FOR_AXIS` carries the
numbers and the measurement; `test_wall_facing` re-measures the staged pixels
every run, so a rebake that turns a wall cannot land quietly again.
THE ATHENIAN BAKES ARE UNUSED. `vis.wall_short/medium/long/gate` (no age
suffix) predate the age ladder and are not in any tier above -- the roster does
not name Athens for walls. Left staged rather than deleted: they are the
obvious stand-in if a fourth tier is ever wanted, and staged art costs nothing
but disk.
THE WALL TOWER IS ALREADY IN THE GAME under another name. The roster's
'Pers/wall_tower (Guard Tower)' and 'rome/wall_tower' are exactly what
`vis.guard_tower` is baked from (achaemenids/wall_tower age 3, romans/wall_tower
age 4), so `building.guard_tower` IS the wall turret and needs nothing. The two
spare `vis.wall_wood_tower_age2/age3` bakes are the germ and brit variants of
the same piece and are unused for the same reason the Athenian set is.
PLACEHOLDER SIZES are the GAMEPLAY footprint in metres (tiles x 2 m), not the
measured mesh -- the reverse of every other entry here. A wall's mesh extent and
its footprint are the same thing to within a rounding, the placeholder only ever
draws if the atlas goes missing, and a diamond the size of the tiles it claims is
the more useful thing to see in that case. Heights are the 0 A.D. template
`<Footprint><Height>` halved to project metres, maxed across the tier's ages:
_note_siege_packed: THE THREE ENGINES HAVE A SECOND ACTOR EACH, and it is the wagon they travel on
before it: these ids were staged on 2026-08-27 and deliberately left undeclared,
because an id referenced by nothing reads a year later as art that failed to land.
CLIP SETS ARE DISJOINT AND THAT IS THE FEATURE. Packed carries idle + walk and no
attack; deployed carries idle + attack and no walk. Neither can do the other's job
and neither has a fold-up clip, so the transition is `pack_ticks` of the new art
standing still -- `AnimationSystem` sends `idle` for it rather than letting the
atlas fall back, which would have played a walk cycle over a stationary engine.
NO COLOUR BAKES, so a tinted onager turns plain the moment it packs. The deployed
onager and trebuchet each carry 8 colour atlases and their packed twins carry none,
so `colours` is absent here rather than false-by-oversight. Filed in
asset_request.md; it is 16 bakes and it is cosmetic, not blocking.
PLACEHOLDER FIGURES ARE THE N FRAME, the same derivation as everything else here
(fx = fy = rect.w / 32, height = (anchor.y - rect.w / 4) / 19.596). Worth knowing:
`vis.ballista` and `vis.onager` above no longer reproduce from their own current
atlases -- they were derived before the 2026-08-27 yaw re-bake and are now off by
about 0.1 m and 0.3 m. Harmless, since a placeholder only draws when the pack is
missing, and recorded so the next person to check does not think they found a bug.
_note_dragon: TWO DRAGON VISUALS, AND `unit.dragon` USES THE RIGGED ONE (2026-09-04).
`vis.dragon` is the original bake off the unrigged 0 A.D. mesh: ONE static
frame, fps 1, loop false, across 8 stored directions. It cannot walk, attack
or die, which is why `unit.dragon` carried `speed: 0` for months -- a moving
unit with one frame slides across the map.
`vis.dragon_rigged` is the same mesh with a commissioned armature, and it
bakes all five clips: idle, walk (Fly2), attack (shootFire), die and decay.
THE STATIC ONE IS KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED, and not out of sentiment: it is
1/50th the size (154 KB against 7.7 MB) and it is the fallback if the rigged
bake ever has to be pulled. Nothing references it today. If it is still
unreferenced when the art pack is built, drop it from the pack -- 7.7 MB is
already the single largest visual in the game.
NEITHER CAN TAKE PLAYER COLOUR, and it was measured rather than assumed:
white against blue at `directions = 1` moved 0 of 5,567 opaque pixels. So
neither carries `colours: true`. That would make two dragons unattributable,
and the answer is that there is only ever ONE: gaia's mother, at the nest,
claimed by killing her (PLAN.md 13.2). Nobody trains a dragon.
_note_dragon_nest: THE DRAGON NEST (PLAN.md 13.2), declared 2026-09-04. THE ART WAS ALREADY BAKED
AND STAGED AND THE GAME SIMPLY COULD NOT SEE IT -- all three atlases sat in
assets/atlases/ with nothing in this file pointing at them, which looks exactly
like art that was never made. Checked file by file rather than trusted: PLAN.md
said 'all three are staged' and that claim has been wrong before.
THE SHRINE IS THE CORE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE TRICK. PLAN.md describes the nest as
'22 bushes and 12 standing stones around a shrine WITH NO CORE' -- there is no
bespoke nest mesh and nobody is going to model one. But EntityView draws an
entity's own visual first and then its props, so a props-only visual would paint a
magenta placeholder in the middle of its own decoration. Making the shrine the
core costs nothing, needs no code, and matches the description: the shrine IS the
thing in the middle.
PROP ORDER IS SCREEN DEPTH, AND THE SORT KEY IS x+y RATHER THAN y. Iso._project
puts screen y at (x + y) * half.y, and EntityView splits behind-the-core from
in-front at `at.y < 0` -- which is x+y < 0, not y < 0. Sorting these by world y
would have got both the split and the back-to-front order wrong, and it would have
looked like a z-order bug in the renderer rather than a bad list.
THE LAYOUT IS TWO RINGS AT ODD COUNTS WITH OFFSET PHASES (13 and 9 bushes against
12 stones) so the overgrowth does not line up with the henge and read as a
pattern. Generated rather than hand-placed; furthest prop is 8.8 m = 4.4 tiles
from centre, which is what sizes building.dragon_nest's footprint.
NAMING DRIFT WORTH KNOWING: PLAN.md's art column says `bush_badlands`, and what
was actually baked is `flora/trees/temperate_bush_biome.xml`. Either is a bush and
nothing depends on which; PLAN.md now names the one that exists.
_note_projectiles: PROJECTILES (PLAN.md 4.13), declared 2026-08-22. All three were staged with the
weapon bakes and referenced by nothing until then -- the same 'staged but never
declared' state the walls were found in, one size smaller, and predicted in
PLAN.md 15 item 7 before it was checked.
THESE IDS ARE ALSO DEF IDS, which nothing else in this file is. A projectile has
no entry in units.json or buildings.json because there is nothing to say about an
arrow beyond which sprite it is: `UnitDef.attack_projectile` names one of these
directly, `SimWorld.spawn_projectile` uses it as the entity's def_id, and
`GameDataRegistry.visual_for` resolves an id that is already a declared visual to
itself rather than there being a fourth def table with one column in it.
WHO THROWS WHAT is in units.json, not here: arrow for the three bow units and the
two ships, bolt for the ballista, stone for the onager and trebuchet. The dragon
throws nothing -- it is range 3 and type pierce and would be handed an arrow by
any rule clever enough to infer one, and it breathes fire.
PLACEHOLDER SIZES are the measured sprite, which for these is genuinely tiny:
arrow 0.09 x 0.75 m, bolt 0.22 x 1.33, stone 0.35 x 0.35, all read off the
atlases' own frame rects at 22.63 px/m. They are the honest figures rather than
useful ones -- a projectile is never selected, so nothing sizes a ring from them,
and the placeholder only ever draws if the art pack is missing.
NO `ages` MAP. An arrow is an arrow in every age, which is the same reason units
carry none (PLAN.md 2.7.1: buildings carry the age, units do not).
_note_waypoint_flag: A MARKER, NOT AN ENTITY -- the only id in this file that no def points at.
Nothing spawns it: `WaypointFlag` is one node GameScene owns and moves to
whichever of your buildings is selected, so it never reaches _visual_id_of()
and `atlas_for` is called by hand. Declared here anyway because that is the
seam's whole contract -- filenames live in this file and nowhere else -- and
because `colours: true` is what buys the eight tints for one boolean.
footprint_m and height_m are MEASURED off the atlas rather than guessed: the
frame is 15 x 67 px at 22.627 px/m, so 0.66 x 0.66 x 2.96 m. That height is
within 4 cm of the 3.0 m pole the procedural placeholder drew, which is the
one number in this entry worth keeping if the art is ever re-cut -- 3 m is
above a villager's head (2.178) and below a house's eaves, and that band is
why the marker reads against both.
The placeholder is a MAST, not a diamond, deliberately: WaypointFlag draws
the tile diamond itself and always has, so a placeholder diamond here would
double it up and say nothing about the pole being missing.
